currentContext.expansion: Tata Communications' expansion is network- and platform-led rather than plant-led. During FY 2025-26 it integrated the new TGN-IA2 (Tata Global Network - Intra-Asia 2) submarine cable system, constructed by the Asia Direct Cable consortium, into its Network Fabric — improving latency, adding redundancy and increasing network diversity through interconnection with the existing TGN-IA. The Network Fabric rests on a round-the-globe subsea optical fibre network of 500,000+ km and an extensive terrestrial fibre network of 200,000+ km, with 650+ transmission Points of Presence integrated into global subsea cable systems and leading data centres, network accessibility across 190+ countries and 70% of global content providers connected to its IP network. Ongoing infrastructure investment is directed at software-defined networking, self-healing dynamic networks, direct cloud connectivity, expanded direct routes to major cloud, SaaS and OTT platforms, and 800G wavelength technologies to carry high-capacity AI traffic between data centres. Platform build-out during the year included the launch of an AI-ready suite — Tata Communications IZO+ Multi Cloud Network, the Tata Communications Edge Distribution Platform and ThreadSpan — plus IZO Data Centre Dynamic Connectivity, the Vayu cloud-to-edge portfolio (Core Infrastructure Services, Developer Platform and Vayu Edge Platform, built in India and governed in India), Next Generation SOCs, and LEO satellite support for IZO+ Internet WAN customers. Inorganic expansion took the form of a majority stake in Commotion, Inc. to strengthen the Interaction Fabric, alongside portfolio pruning (divestment of NetFoundry Inc.). Geographic expansion into China came through a 50:50 joint venture, TC (Shanghai) Technology Company Limited, incorporated effective 12 March 2026 between Tata Communications (Hong Kong) Limited and Shanghai Runshengtong Management Consulting Co., Ltd., and a wholly-owned TC (Shanghai) Network Services Company Limited incorporated with effect from 18 April 2025. No rupee capex plan, project cost or commissioning schedule is stated in the narrative chapters; the only rupee quantum in this bundle is the capital-commitments named disclosure.

The standalone debt-equity ratio rose to 0.45x from 0.31x, an increase management attributes mainly to borrowings availed during the year, while interest coverage fell to 5.19x from 6.78x.

risks.risk: Talent shortage, attrition and reskilling gap (Talent Risk in the register)
risks.note: A skilled workforce is vital in the evolving digital environment; talent shortages, higher attrition and inadequate upskilling may impact growth, business continuity and competitive positioning. Mitigation rests on attraction of skilled professionals for critical roles, learning and capability development, attrition management and a structured succession framework.

risks.risk: Regulatory uncertainty across a global footprint
risks.note: Evolving data regulations, data-localisation and digital-sovereignty requirements and global geopolitical developments continue to affect supply chains, compliance requirements and operational flexibility across markets; the Company's global footprint necessitates enhanced oversight and governance to ensure adherence to local regulations in every jurisdiction it serves.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The statutory auditor carried an Emphasis of Matter: the Company has received Show Cause-cum-Demand Notices from the Department of Telecommunications towards licence fee on Adjusted Gross Revenue for financial years ranging from FY 2005-06 to FY 2024-25 and has disclosed H 7,513.71 crores as contingent liability. Individual demands (H875.80 crore, H992 crore, H6,159 crore, and others) are contested before TDSAT, which has directed DoT not to take coercive action pending final disposal; matters remain pending adjudication and DoT's cross-appeals sit before the Supreme Court. An adverse outcome would be material relative to annual profit.
- Indian tax authorities have not accepted certain historical tax-holiday and expense claims and in a few instances have sought penalties; disallowances and penalties are at various stages of appeal. Management states that although no appeal has been finally decided against the Company, in the unlikely event all disputes were decided against it there could be adverse financial implications on the business.
- Global slowdown, inflation, rising interest rates, currency volatility, trade tariffs and geopolitical uncertainty may affect operations across multiple geographies. Early-warning indicators reviewed during the year included potential tariff changes in the United States and Mexico, Indo-Pak tensions, China's rare-earth export controls, instability in the Middle East and the Red Sea cable cut incident. Management also flags that geopolitical conflict could disrupt subsea cables and global routes, slow economic growth and delay IT investment.
- Traffic migration and revenue continuity may be affected if alternate cable capacity is not made available in a timely manner. Separately, subsea cable disruptions such as the recent Red Sea cable cuts can cause latency spikes, traffic rerouting, temporary service degradation, higher operating costs and increased network vulnerability. Mitigation relies on alternate routes, backup capacity and prioritised capacity enhancement — all of which carry capital cost.
- Growing data exchange across expanding digital ecosystems and accelerating AI adoption increase exposure to cyber threats, data breaches and system vulnerabilities. Because the Company both operates critical network infrastructure and sells security services, a breach carries direct financial, regulatory and reputational consequences. Compliance obligations include the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 and other applicable privacy laws.
- Rapid advances in Agentic AI, quantum computing, network APIs and multi-modal, data-centric networking require continuous innovation and upgrades. Ineffective integration of AI and emerging technologies into products and processes, insufficient reskilling, and evolving regulatory standards could adversely impact operational resilience, compliance, service reliability and long-term competitive advantage. An AI Committee has been constituted to oversee governance, compliance and technology integration.
- Despite rising data consumption, sector revenue growth remains moderate with pricing pressure and high capital investment weighing on profitability. EBITDA margin at 19.4% was marginally lower because of the mix shift toward higher-growth digital services, and management states that achieving sustainable profitability in digital services will require continued scale, cost optimisation and disciplined execution of product roadmaps — i.e. the growth engine is currently margin-dilutive.
- Foreign currency volatility, interest rate fluctuations and dependence on external capital markets may influence financial stability; the Company hedges with derivative instruments and monitors net debt to EBITDA. The standalone debt-equity ratio rose to 0.45x from 0.31x, an increase management attributes mainly to borrowings availed during the year, while interest coverage fell to 5.19x from 6.78x.

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.
